title: Intelligent Tutors Beyond K-12: An Observational Study of Adult Learner Engagement and Academic Impact
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether intelligent tutoring systems, which are often evaluated in K-12 settings, can also support adult learners when used voluntarily as a supplementary resource. The authors focus on a gap in the literature: how adult students adopt and engage with tutoring tools outside of mandatory classroom use, and whether that engagement is associated with measurable learning gains.

The intervention studied is Apprentice Tutors, a novel intelligent tutoring platform for College Algebra. The system provides adaptive problem selection through Bayesian Knowledge Tracing, immediate correctness feedback, multi-layered hints, progress tracking, and integration with learning management systems. The study analyzes two years of deployment metadata, grades, and demographic records from adult learners at a 2-year state technical college. Students could use the tutors optionally in Blackboard or Canvas, making the context a real-world, voluntary, supplemental use case.

The study finds that only a minority of enrolled students used the tutors, but those who did were more likely to be female and slightly older on average. Tutor use peaked in the evenings and on Thursdays, suggesting that adult learners used the system outside typical work hours and in advance of assessments. Within the tutor, error rates decreased with practice, and across the course, tutor users earned slightly higher unit assessment scores. Because the design is observational, the authors do not claim causality, but they conclude that intelligent tutors appear viable for adult learners and may support both in-system learning and classroom performance.
quality_tier_rationale: This is an observational, quasi-experimental study without randomization or a control condition, so causal credibility is limited. It is nevertheless a peer-reviewed empirical analysis with multiple linked data sources and regression/learning-curve modeling, which is stronger than opinion-only evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests modest positive learning and engagement effects, but the evidence is correlational and effect sizes are small or not fully reported. Because the study focuses on adult learners rather than K-12 priority populations, the impact signal is promising but unclear for the requested K-12 evidence framing.

interventions.use_case: voluntary supplemental algebra tutoring for adult college learners, with adaptive problem selection via Bayesian Knowledge Tracing, real-time correctness feedback, multi-layer hints, and mastery tracking

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports within-tutor learning gains in College Algebra, with student error rates decreasing as practice opportunities increased in Apprentice Tutors. The authors describe this as evidence of skill improvement in knowledge components, with the learning curve fit showing p<0.001; exact effect size was not reported.
finding.measure: Error rates across skill practice opportunities; knowledge component mastery/learning curve in the tutor
finding.study_size: n=3,510 enrolled; n=520 tutor users; n=214 Unit 1 tutor users
finding.confidence_interval: 95% CI shown graphically for the learning curve, but exact numeric CI not reported

finding.finding_summary: Tutor users earned slightly higher mean grades on Unit 1 assessments than non-users, and number of tutor transactions was positively associated with grade in a linear regression. The regression coefficient for Transactions was 0.26 (SE=0.08, t=3.39, p<0.001), but the paper does not report a standardized effect size or causal estimate.
finding.study_size: n=3,510; analysis focused on n=214 Unit 1 tutor users

finding.finding_summary: The study found substantial voluntary engagement with the tutor among adult learners, with usage concentrated in evenings and late nights, suggesting the system supported flexible participation around work-life constraints. However, this is descriptive and correlational evidence rather than an experimental measure of motivation or persistence.
finding.measure: Tutor usage patterns by day/time; voluntary adoption rate
